text: Spore Screen is an armor Augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X that nullifies the debuffs from spore weather. The Skell equivalent is Weather.SPORE-RES.

Stagger is a mobility debuff in Xenoblade Chronicles X. An enemy or party member inflicted with Stagger will be shoved back a short distance. If they are in the middle of casting an Art, the animation will be interrupted. Enemies cannot act until Stagger wears off. Similar to Break in Xenoblade Chronicles, an enemy or party member inflicted with Stagger will lose their resistance to Topple. If the enemy is sufficiently large, a Skell can Bind them.

Story Exclusive Enemies are special enemies in and . They are story related minor enemies that the party is either forced to fight, like a mini-boss, or apply assistance to or summoned by Bosses. As such, they are (usually) limited and only appear during story related events, they can only be defeated once per playthrough like for the Quest Exclusive Enemies. Unlike Bosses, Story Exclusive Enemies have a normal target window frame when looking at them. However they are fought like Bosses, that is to say the battle arena is fenced by a green field barrier (if the arena is not physically limited), they do not usually drop Treasure Chest. Stream Edge (Japanese: , Sutorīmu Ejji) is one of Shulk's physical arts in and . It is a frontal area attack that inflicts damage and Break to enemies within 8 meters. The Talent Gauge is filled by 15% for each enemy hit.
Spraine is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles 2. He is a salvager who can be found at Goldmouth Exit Dock in the Argentum Trade Guild and aboard the C.S.E.V. Maelstrom.
Stratospheric Thunder (Japanese: ) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Zeke's arts when using the Big Bang Edge.
Steady Drill (Japanese: , Gungun doriru) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Tora's arts when using a Drill Shield.
Steamwork Organs are Instrument Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Adelno Music in Alba Cavanich in the Empire of Mor Ardain. They are one of the favorite Pouch items of Mòrag and Ursula.
Sprack Parisax (Japanese: , Supikku Parasu) are enemies in . They are members of the Parisax family, and can be found at level 35 - 37 at the entrance to the Dragon's Stomach in the Kingdom of Uraya.

Store Deeds are Key Items in . They can be purchased to grant permanent upgrades. Once every other item a shop has been bought at least once, and the player exits and reenters the shop menu, the deed will be available. Most stores do not have their entire selection available from the start, requiring a high enough Development Level to be reached and certain Merc Missions to be completed. However, Accessory shops, Aux Core shops, Core Chip shops, Cylinder shops, Exchange shops, Information shops, Inns, and Other shops never offer their deeds for sale.

The Spraywater Caverns (Japanese: , Himatsu no Dōkutsu) are a location in . It is located in the right area of the upper level of Gormott Province, directly north of Sauros's Bed. There are no enemies here.

The Starboard Balcony (Japanese: , Ugen Chūō Dekki) is a landmark in . It is an external balcony aboard the Titan Battleship in the Gormott Province, beside the Guardroom and beyond the Battle Command.
The Sternum Arch (Japanese: , Daikyōkotsu no Āchi) is a landmark in . It is located in the Head of the Kingdom of Uraya, between Jebbas Outlook and the Great Blowhole.

The Stone Gate Ruins (Japanese: , Kuzureta Iwakado) are a landmark in . They are located in the Stomach of Uraya, between Drillbore Bridge and Funnystone Highway. A path leading north-west from here reaches the Old Quarry and Loska's Gap. There is a Treasure Trove here containing Gold and a Spinel Chip.

The Spirit Crucible Entrance (Japanese: , Erupisu Reidō Iriguchi) is a landmark in . It is the first location on the Upper Level of Spirit Crucible Elpys, leading on to the Canyon of Husks. There are no enemies here, although there is a Traveling Bard in the New Game Plus.

The Stele of Judgment (Japanese: , Shinpan no Ishibumi) is a landmark in . It is located on the Lower Level of Spirit Crucible Elpys, between the Chamber of Offering and the Chamber of Pillars. Perun's Heart-to-heart, "Indomitable Will", can be found here. There are no enemies here.

The Storage Area Entrance (Japanese: , Kakunō Eria Iriguchi) is a Landmark in . It is located on the Lower Level of the First Low Orbit Station. It is connected to the Architect's Room via an elevator. The Heart-to-Heart "Daybreak" is located here.

The Streets (Japanese: , Shigai) of the Land of Morytha are a level in . It is the first area of the Land of Morytha visited, leading on to the Decaying Titan. There are two Heart-to-hearts here; "Mythra Vs. Brighid" and "Morytha the Unknown".

Spring-Shower Elliott (Japanese: , Harusame no Esukāto) is a Unique Monster in . He is a Driver and can be found at level 42 patrolling up and down the spiral Lumos Pillar in the Kingdom of Tantal. He is the brother of Autumn-Shower Melvin. When defeated, he drops the Letter to Melvin, allowing Autumn-Shower Melvin to be fought further up the pillar at his grave.
The Storage Warehouse (Japanese: , Busshi Kakunōko) is a Location in . It is located on the Upper Level of the Empire of Mor Ardain.
Steamflake Tabboulehs are Veggie Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Griogair's Greens in Alba Cavanich in the Empire of Mor Ardain. They are one of the favorite Pouch items of Azami.
Steamed Milk Brioches are Dessert Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Salter Sweets in Alba Cavanich in the Empire of Mor Ardain.
Steam-Gel Ice Creams are Dessert Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Salter Sweets in Alba Cavanich in the Empire of Mor Ardain.
Steamed Bluegills are Seafood Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Ikthus Fishmongers in Fonsa Myma in the Kingdom of Uraya.
The Sprintsy Deeds are Store Deeds in . They can be purchased from Sprintsy Sweets in Fonsa Myma in the Kingdom of Uraya.
Steamed Veg Stralus are Veggie Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Lectica Vegetables in Theosoir in the Kingdom of Tantal. They are one of the favorite Pouch items of Theory.
Steamy Oils are Cosmetic Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Praximo Cosmetics in Theosoir in the Kingdom of Tantal.
Steam Powders are Cosmetic Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Praximo Cosmetics in Theosoir in the Kingdom of Tantal.
Sprintsy Sweets is a shop in . It is run by Karundle and can be found in Fonsa Myma in the Kingdom of Uraya. It is specialized in Desserts.

Squoods (Japanese: , Suīdo) are a family of enemies in . They are gigantic squid-like creatures that appear after Salvaging or during odd weather condition (such as mist in the Kingdom of Tantal). All Squoods are green except for the Challenge Battle Mode version of Cloud Sea King Ken, who has a red head.
Steady Beam (Japanese: , Janjan bīmu) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Tora's arts when using a Variable Saber and grants self heal. Tora shoots a five-directional laser beam out of the saber.
Storm Spin (Japanese: ) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Rex's arts when using Whipswords.

Spring Eks (Japanese: , Supuringu Ekusu) are enemies in . They are members of the Eks family, and can be found at level 3-12 on the Upper Level - Right of the Gormott Province, particularly on Garanti Plain.

Spirit Lexos (Japanese: , Supiritto Rekusosu) are enemies in . They are members of the Lexos family. One can be found at level 60-62 by the 7th Perimeter Skyport in the World Tree. These have a 30% resistance to Break. Four must be defeated to unlock Brighid's level 3 "Fire Mastery", Newt's level 4 Extreme Gutsy Spirit and Gorg's level 5 "FAS".

|-|XC2 = |-|TTGC = Steel Salmons are Fish collectibles in and . They can be found in the Gormott Province at various Collection Points and by Salvaging at any Gormott Salvage Point. In the , Steel Salmons can also be obtained by scanning an amiibo.
Steel Pipe Lexos are Art Pouch items in . They can be purchased at Talmye Antiques in Fonsett Village in the Leftherian Archipelago.

Stark Aspars (Japanese: , Sutōku Angu) are enemies in . They are members of the Aspar family, and can be found at level 45-47 at the Wonder Spring Plaza Ruins on the Upper Level of the Spirit Crucible Elpys.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Spring Shoes (Japanese: , Supuringu Shūzu) are accessories in and . They increase the wearer's Agility stat by up to 17. They are the upgraded version of the Wolf Shoes accessory. For a similar multiplicative effect that can stack with this gear, check the Shell Shoes, Assassin Shoes, Ester Shoes and Dauntless Boots accessories. Other sources of Agility apply before this fixed stat bonus.
Split-Hop Gizmos are Tree collectibles in . They can be found on the World Tree. In the , Split-Hop Gizmos can also be obtained by scanning an amiibo.
Sporefruits are Vegetable collectibles in . They can be found in the Spirit Crucible Elpys.
Stained Pipes are Mechanical collectibles in . They can be found in Temperantia.

Starry Persimmons are Vegetable collectibles in . They can be found on the World Tree, in particular right next to the 7th Perimeter Skyport Skip Travel point. In the , Starry Persimmons can also be obtained by scanning an amiibo.

Stream Navies are Fish collectibles in . They can be found in the Leftherian Archipelago, in particular from Collection Points on the southeast and northwest sides of Baldotas Isle. Ten are needed to unlock Corvin's level 3 Alae Custodiae.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Spirit Tree Wards are accessories in and . They increase the HP restored to the wearer when they are revived by up to 39% of their maximum HP. They are the upgraded version of the Grandarbor Ward accessory. The World Tree Ward accessory offers a stronger instance of this equipment's effect. It can stack with the additive HP recovering effects of a teammate's Friendship Ring, Affection Ring or Promise Ring accessories.
Spiral Uppercut (Japanese: ) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Mòrag's arts when using Megalance.
Stratospheric Hoops are Treasure items in . They can be obtained through Salvaging at Jubilee Gate at the Cliffs of Morytha. One is needed during Souvenirs from Morytha.
Starlight Pedestals are Treasure items in . They can be obtained through Salvaging at the 7th Perimeter Skyport on the World Tree.

Steel Chips are Core Chips in and . They can be bought from Shroomblade Smithing or dropped by a wide variety of enemies, mainly in the Empire of Mor Ardain. Steel Chips share their appearance with Cobalt Chips, Gold Chips and Iron Chips. __TOC__

Stonic Urchons (Japanese: , Sutoniku Unin) are enemies in . They are members of the Urchon family, and can be found at level 40-43 at the Isle of Urchon in the Leftherian Archipelago, or at level 43-45 at Little Garden of Tradition and in the Cloudway in the Leftherian Archipelago. Some level 43-45 Stonic Urchons can be summoned by Perplexed Stoyan when using its art "Mega Wave".
Stellar Scouts (Japanese: , Suterā Sukauto) are enemies in . They are members of Brionac that can be found at level 57-61 at the Brionac Occupied Zone in the Empire of Mor Ardain.

The Spoot Driver (Japanese: , Supūto Doraibā) is a quest-exclusive enemy in . He is a Driver enemy fought at level 51 at the Lost Capital Judicium in Temperantia during Blade-Sharp Memory. He and the Grep Driver apply assistance alongside to the quest-exclusive boss Vengeful Waldemar.

Sting Runners (Japanese: , Sutingu Rannā) are enemies in . They are Sovereigns, and only one can be found at level 62-64 on Lv. 3, Alioth in the World Tree (on the north side, accompanied by one Familion Sovereign). Four of them must be defeated to unlock Herald's level 3 "Electric Mastery", and two of them must be defeated to unlock T-elos's Level 5 "Heaven's Tracker".
Stolen Keepsake is a quest in . It can be received from Dragand in the Village Guardian of the Leftherian Archipelago.
Stench is an Info Item in . It can be purchased from the Informant shop in the Argentum Trade Guild.
Spitt Pods (Japanese: , Supitto Poddo) are enemies in . They are Arachno Pods that can be found at level 29-34 in the Old Industrial District on the Upper Level of the Empire of Mor Ardain.

Strange Minerals are Key Items in . They are obtained by using Agate's "Prospecting" field skill at various Agate's Mining points after starting Precious Yearnings. During the quest, they can be appraised by Misimisi to determine what they are, as well as to advance the quest and unlock higher levels of Agate's skill.

The Stormstone is a Key Item in . It is received from Misimisi during Precious Yearnings by having him appraise a Strange Mineral from a prospecting point near the Old Plumbing Entrance in the Empire of Mor Ardain. Upon appraisal, Misimisi responds with, "Yes yes yes..This mineral called Stormstone. Stormstone occasionally create mini tornado windy effect. Quite popular in hot springs of Mor Ardain. Sink stone in water and pleasant bubbles rise up from below!"

The Starboard Deck (Japanese: , Ugen Kanpan) is a location in . It is located on the Titan Battleship in Gormott Province, accessible from the Bridge. There is a Treasure Trove here. There are no enemies here.
The Storage Room (Japanese: , Busshi Hokanko) is a Location in . It is located in Theoscaldia Palace in the Kingdom of Tantal.

Straat Serpronds (Japanese: , Sutoraito Rodon) are enemies in . They are members of the Serprond family, and can be found at level 56-60 at the 7th Perimeter Skyport on the Mid Level of the World Tree after Salvaging.

The Steamflake Contract is a Key Item in . It is received as a reward after completing the Merc Mission White and Cold. It enables the purchase of Steamflake Tabbouleh from the Griogair's Greens shop at Alba Cavanich in the Empire of Mor Ardain.

The Stralu Contract is a Key Item in . It is received as a reward after completing the Merc Mission Nopon Cooking. It enables the purchase of Fragrant Samod Stralu from the Speck Butchers shop at Fonsett Village in the Leftherian Archipelago.

Stolen Data is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Empire of Mor Ardain during the quest Hard to Stomach. The time required to complete this mission is 40 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 10 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Electric Mastery", "Keen Eye" and "Clairvoyant Eye" Field Skills. The Top Secret Papers information can be alternatively bought from the Informant Durmagh with 2,000 G, making this mission optional.
The Square Tablet Piece is a Key Item in . It is obtained at the Great Pillar Passage on the Lower Level of the Kingdom of Tantal during the quest Lost Kingdom.
Stormstarter (Japanese: , Sutōmukōzā, Lit. "Storm Causer") is a Driver Art in . It is one of Rex's arts when using a Sword Tonfa. This art recycles Rex's Bullet Punch.

Standing Ovation (Japanese: ) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Zeke's arts when using a Calamity Scythe. It can be obtained upon New Game Plus, after finishing the game and installing Patch (Ver.1.3.0). This art recycles Zeke's Raging Charge.

Stoking the Fire (Japanese: ) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Mòrag's arts when using Infinity Fans. It can be obtained upon New Game Plus, after finishing the game and installing Patch (Ver.1.3.0). This art recycles Mòrag's Revolution Flash.

Stark Artillery (Japanese: ) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Zeke's arts when using a Decimation Cannon. It can be obtained upon New Game Plus, after finishing the game and installing Patch (Ver.1.3.0). This art recycles Zeke's Blowback Cannon.

Stippon is an NPC in . He is a Leftherian who can be found walking around the Fonsett Residential Area near the Fonsett Arch in the Leftherian Archipelago at night. He offers the Merc Mission Night Visitors.

Strike Mod is a Role CPU in . It grants Poppi an Attacker role with average defenses and aggro generation. It offers a modifier that increases Tora's Dexterity stat by a percentage. It specializes in maximizing accuracy, and can be used to customize Poppi QT and Poppi QTπ. Poppi α is not compatible with this part. __TOC__
Stidias is an NPC in . Stidias is a Tantalese who can be found at Theoscaldia Palace in the Kingdom of Tantal. Stidias offers the Merc Mission Ice Hunter.
The Storied Band is a Key Item in . It can be obtained on the ground near the base of Amphoret Pillar in the Kingdom of Tantal during the quest The Writer's Assistant.

The Steel Pipe Contract is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles 2. It is received as a reward after completing a Merc Mission. It enables the purchase of an item from the Talmye Antiques shop in the Leftherian Archipelago.
The Stolen Parcel is a Key Item in . It must be retrieved during Our Daily Bread for Kupon, from a group of Tirkin at the Tirkin Turf. It must be delivered to Tilly Bakery.
The Splendid Ancient Tome is a Key Item in . It can be obtained from Reedirait Bookstore in the Argentum Trade Guild during the Merc Mission Adenine's Password during the quest Limits of Awareness.

Spotted Parisax (Japanese: , Supotto Parasu) are three quest-exclusive enemies in . They are members of the Parisax family that are fought at level 30 at the Dragon's Stomach in the Kingdom of Uraya during the quest The Titan Scholar.
The Spirit Crucible Elpys Salvage Points are places in the Spirit Crucible Elpys in where salvaging can be performed. There are two Salvage Points in Spirit Crucible Elpys.

Spoot Eks (Japanese: , Supitto Ekusu) are Challenge Battle Enemies in . They are members of the Eks family that are fought at level 28 during the Challenge Battle Grazing Flock. This enemy drops no items.

Spoony Aligos (Japanese: , Supūnī Diburo) are Challenge Battle Enemies in . They are members of the Aligo family, and can be found at level 60 during the second and third waves of the Challenge Battle Panic at the Seaside. This enemy drops no items.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Staunch Boots (Japanese: , Forutsa Būtsu) are DLC accessories in . They increase damage dealt against toppled enemies by up to 135%. They are the upgraded version of Mechanized Greaves, Crystal Greaves and Graphite Greaves accessories. They can be found in the Land of Challenge from Treasure Troves obtained after completing a Challenge Battle, available as downloadable content from the Challenge Battle Mode Pack of the Expansion Pass.
Steel Brand (Japanese: ) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Mòrag's arts when using a Monado. This art recycles Mòrag's Vajra Blow.

The Stopper Sovereigns (Japanese: , Shīringu Roiyaru) are six quest-exclusive enemies in . They are Sovereigns that are fought at level 95-96 at the Highway 8 in the Land of Morytha during Mystery Launch Codes. One of the three enemies drops the Access Code 1 upon defeat. A second group of three must then be fought at the Great Wall Tunnel No. 8, where one of them holds the Access Code 2.
Starfall (Japanese: , Sutāfōru) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Rex's arts when wielding an Uchigatana. This art recycles Rex's Breakdown.

The Streamsand Corridor (Japanese: , Ryūsha no Kairō) is a location in . It is located in the center of the Dannagh Region of the Kingdom of Torna, beside the Dannagh Desert. There is a Collection Point here, and the key items Golden Sand Cocoons must be collected here during A Small Promise. The Golden Monster Mesmer Tlaloc appears here after its location is purchased from the Nopon Halfsage for 400,000 G.
The Strategy Room is a location in . It is located in the southwestern area of Gormott, as part of the Ardainian battleship moored at Lascham Cove. There are several Treasure Troves here.

Steeky Hoxes (Japanese: , Sutikkī Hoggusu) are enemies in . They are members of the Hox family and can be found at level 4-9 in the Lasaria Region of the Kingdom of Torna, particularly at Haradd Hills, Yanchik Harbor and Uccar's Trail.
Spring Revival Perfumes are Fragrance items in . They can be created by Brighid at Campsites.
Steel Salmon Tempuras are Seafood Pouch Items in . They can be created by Aegaeon at Campsites.
Sticky Stick Insects are Insect collectible items in . They can be found in Gormott. Alongside Memento Bark, they are required for every Script Minoth can make with Dramaturgy.

Standards (Japanese: , Furaggu) are a family of enemies in the . They are also named Symbols (Japanese: , Shinboru) or Emblems (Japanese: , Enburemu). They are stationary war flags, also known as standards, belonging to groups of enemies - Garluses, Brionac, Agnian and Kevesi soldiers, or Ignas. Standards buff them in a similar manner to Totems belonging to Tirkin.

Story Missions are a type of mission in . They are related directly to the story and always accepted in the Interior of the BLADE Barracks. There are 12 Story Missions, with each corresponding to a chapter in the storyline. Each one has specific conditions that must be met in order to begin the next Story Mission. All Story Missions after Chapter 3 include the requirement that Elma and Lin be in the party (In Chapters 1-3, they are automatically accepted after the previous, and Elma and Lin are always in the party then), and certain characters cannot be in the party for certain chapters. Once begun, they cannot be abandoned, and no new Affinity Missions may be started until the Story Mission

Starslash (Japanese: , Rokka, "Snow"/lit. "Six Flowers") is one of Jin's Vanguard Arts in . When used, Jin poses then does a diagonal right downward slash, then a diagonal right upward slash, then a diagonal left downward slash.
Steady on, Grandad! (Japanese: , Jicchan wo Tasukete!) is a quest in . It can be received at the Grand Arch in Gran Dell Bionis' Shoulder from Miles, after Gran Dell is attacked by Fogbeasts.

Starchy Knapsacks are light legs armour in Xenoblade Chronicles: Definitive Edition. They can be obtained as rewards after clearing the Time Attack challenge Shaggy-Dog Story. They can only be worn by Riki.
Sprout Knapsacks are light legs armour in Xenoblade Chronicles: Future Connected. They are part of Kino's initial equipment and can only be worn by him.
Sprout Vests are light torso armour in Xenoblade Chronicles: Future Connected. They are part of Kino's initial equipment and can only be worn by him.
Prime Sport Glasses are Casual Wear head armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are manufactured by Sakuraba Industries.
Starburst (Japanese: , Sutābāsuto) is Pneuma's Level I Blade Special in .

Starlight Strike (Japanese: , Lit. "Starlight Knee") is Lora and Haze's Level IV Blade Special in . If Starlight Strike is activated by Lora, the special's element will be determined by the Battle Braid she has equipped.
Spiral Snare (Japanese: , Rasenmusubi) is Lora's Level III Special in . As with Lora's other specials, the element of Spiral Snare is determined by the Battle Braid she has equipped.
Storm Edge (Japanese: , Sutōmu Ejji) is Sever's Level I Blade Special in . With the weapon in "tonfa form", Sever conjures a tornado in front of him.
Sprout Hair Ties are light head armour in Xenoblade Chronicles: Future Connected. They are part of Kino's initial equipment and can only be worn by him.
Sprout Amulets are light arms armour in Xenoblade Chronicles: Future Connected. They are part of Kino's initial equipment and can only be worn by him.
Sprout Anklets are light feet armour in Xenoblade Chronicles: Future Connected. They are part of Kino's initial equipment and can only be worn by him.
Stalker (Japanese: , Genkyūshi, Phantom Archer) is an Agnian Attacker class in .
Spocked Aligos (Japanese: , Supokkudo Diburo) are enemies in . They are members of the Aligo family, and can be found at level 27-28 at the Great Cotte Falls.
Strategos (Japanese: , Senryakushi) is an Agnian Healer class in .

Stately Doramma (Japanese: , Butai no Doranma) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Quarmu family, and can be found at level 64 at the Cotte Fountainhead on Great Cotte Falls. It forms the "Aquatic Beasts" duo with Saberly Dorampé. The Scattered Healing Skill can be earned for the Soulhacker class by defeating it.

Still, Move Forward! is a track from , composed by Kenji Hiramatsu. It is track nineteen of disc four on the Xenoblade 2 Original Soundtrack. This music is heard whenever the party engages an enemy in battle at the Cliffs of Morytha, the Land of Morytha, and the World Tree. In the , this song also plays when the party fights the trio of Rooka Ansels during The Home of the Soul, and also during Merc Assault missions when Fever Time is active. The song also appears as a music track in , where it can be played while playing on Gaur Plain and the Cloud Sea of Alrest as well as on Final Destination and the three variants of Battlefield. A motif from this song is used in "New Battle!!!" in .

Spiral Savate (Japanese: , Supairaru Sobatto) is a Battle Art used by Malos in . It is learnt at level 6, but it can't be used by Malos while he's in the party because his arts cannot be changed. With the weapon in "tonfa form", Malos spins clockwise before jumping, performing a horizontal right spin hook kick.
Sweaty Cloths are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be dropped by various Hodes in Makna Forest, or be traded for.

This page lists all the quests available in Sword Valley. Note that these are all timed surprise quests, and will become unavailable after reaching the end of Mechonis Field. Terms and abbreviations are explained in the legend at the bottom of the page.
The Sword Valley Collection is a portion of the Collectopaedia in .

Sturdy Armour (Japanese: , Ganjōna Sōkō) is a common material in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can only be dropped by Flavel Andos found in Eryth Sea, or traded for in Alcamoth. According to their description, it would probably take 6 months to make them wearable. Six pieces are needed for The Deciphering Machine, and four for the reconstruction of Colony 6. In Definitive Edition, they can be purchased in Time Attack place from Nopon Archsage for 700 Noponstones.
Suzanna (Japanese: ) is a Homs in . She can be found in the western portion of the Residential District of Colony 9, southwest from Tranquil Square.
Superbosses are Unique Monsters or Tyrant enemies in the that typically appear at or above the player level cap, or are unlocked during the final chapter of their respective game.

Summon Bolt (Japanese: , Samon Boruto) is one of Melia's summon arts in and . It increases Melia's and nearby allies' Ether by 20% for each active bolt element. Discharging the bolt element delivers a thunderbolt attack with extremely high damage to one enemy.

Strong Dandelions (Japanese: , Popontanpopo) are collectables in . They can be found around Tephra Hill in Colony 9. According to their description, they are known for their small black petals and their roots make a throat medicine.

Sunflower Rogues (Japanese: , Himawari Rōgu) are collectables in . They can be found in Satorl Marsh. According to their description, they only bloom in the wild and they wither the moment they are plucked.

Sweet Peppers (Japanese: , Suwīto Papurika) are collectables in . They can be found in Mechonis Field and Colony 6. According to their description, they are sweet fruits that are often thought as vegetables by mistake.

Sweet Limes (Japanese: , Amaama Raimu) are collectables in . They can be found in Agniratha and Colony 6. According to their description, they are limes that feel like chewing lumps of sugar when eaten.

Swift Zektol (Japanese: , Shippū no Zekutōru) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Volff family, and can be found at level 28 in southern Satorl Marsh, just east of Igna Territory. It can drop the Fancy Volff Hides needed for Making Camp.

Sunlight Schvaik (Japanese: , Yōkō no Shuvaiku) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Rhogul family, and can be found at level 30 during the daytime in the Barren Moor of Satorl Marsh. It has a large wandering range that covers over half of the Barren Moor, including a visit to the Silent Obelisk. Defeating it is the objective of the quest Zazadan Still in Danger. It can drop a Rhogul Axe Crest, three of which are needed for Bridge Repair.

Swimming Cream is light arms armour in . They can be dropped by Cute Brogs. They are part of the Swimming set of armour along with the Swimming Gel, Swimming Oil, Swimming Trunks and Swimming Sandals.
Swimming Bottoms are light legs armour in Xenoblade Chronicles.

Swimming Oil (Japanese: , suimā oiru, lit. swimmer oil) is light torso armour in . It is the second type of swimming costume armour available, and unlike the Bikini set, can be used by both males and females. It can be dropped by various enemies, obtained as a quest reward after completing Liliana's Sincere Request, or be traded for with Miller.
Swimming Tops are light torso armour in Xenoblade Chronicles.
Swep Gauntlets are medium arms armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by the Sunlight Schvaik, and be obtained as a quest reward after completing various quests.
Swep Gear (Japanese: , Suweppu Gia) is medium head armour in Xenoblade Chronicles.
Swep Boots are medium feet armour in . They can be obtained as quest rewards after completing various quests.
Styptic Leggings are medium legs armour in Xenoblade Chronicles.
Survivor Shoes are medium feet armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are not dropped by enemies and can only be obtained from two shops.

Sword Drive (Japanese: , Sōdopairu) is one of Reyn's physical arts in . An enemy hit with this attack will take substantial damage and be knocked back a small distance. It will have a substantial increase in damage if successively used after Berserker and Magnum Charge. In , Nene can use this art.
Sweet Nectar is a rare material in . It is dropped by low level Skeeters in Colony 9, and can be traded for with Miller.

The Supply Convoy (Japanese: , Hokyū Butai Saizensen) is a landmark in . It is located in Sword Valley, between Bionis' Thumb and Ged Fortress. When the party arrives here, they find that Alvis has arranged for Dickson and a small group of Defence Force soldiers to meet them, offering supplies and Anti-Mechon Weapons and armour. Once the party has explained to Dickson what has happened to them since last they met, he and Alvis leave, returning to Bionis to further the war efforts. The Supply Convoy Shop remains here permanently, and there is also an Earth Ether Gear beside it.

※ The outcome is determined by the choice from Ingredients For A Brew. Sweet Seduction (Japanese: , Ama~i Yūwaku) is a quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be received from Migaga at the Sacred Altar in Frontier Village. Once accepted, Kofuko must be spoken to which triggers the quest Ingredients For A Brew. This later quest must be first finished in order to complete Sweet Seduction, two routes are possible and will imply a different gem reward as well as a different result.
Super Cruiser (Japanese: , Sūpākurūzā) is a weapon in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a gunlance wielded by Reyn.

Stunted Growth (Japanese: , Seichōsuru tameni) is a quest in . It can be received from Orkatix at the northeast ledge of the Hidden Machina Village in the Fallen Arm after the Mechonis Core event. Dunban will have to be the party leader to receive this quest. Upon receiving this quest, three additional quests with the required item as the quest name will be triggered. Successfully completing this quest will unlock Dunban's fifth skill branch - Enthusiasm.
Swallow Blades (Japanese: , Tsubame Sōken) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are twin blades wielded by Fiora.

Sun Staves (Japanese: , Taiyō no Tsue) are weapons in and . They are staves that can be wielded by Melia. Among all of her staves in the main game, they have the highest boost to Physical Defense, and are tied with the Dragon Rod Alcar and Alcor Staff for the highest boost to Ether Defense. They also boast the highest block rate and a very high critical rate. In , they are the staves with the almost all highest attributes, the exception being the Meteor Staves which have a higher maximum attack value. __TOC__
Swimming Gel (Japanese: , Suimā Jeru) is light head armour in . It is dropped by several enemies around Colony 9.

Swimming Trunks are light legs armour in . They can be dropped by the Lake Magdalena. They are part of the Swimming set of armour along with the Swimming Gel, Swimming Oil, Swimming Cream and Swimming Sandals.

Supplies for Satorl (Japanese: , Zatōru e no Busshi) is a quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be received by Elior, lying near the pond outside the Refugee Camp on Bionis' Leg. If Melia is in the active party, she will comment.

Summon Ice (Japanese: , Samon Aisu) is one of Melia's summon arts in and . It reduces Ether damage taken by Melia and her allies by 15% for each active ice element. When the ice element is discharged, it damages enemies surrounding Melia and inflicts a Chill status, delivering an additional 60% damage every 2 seconds.

Summon Earth (Japanese: , Samon Āsu) is one of Melia's summon arts in and . Each earth element summoned will reduce Physical damage taken by Melia and her allies within the area effect. When the earth element is discharged, the targeted enemy is inflicted with Poison, doing damage every 2 seconds.

The Swan Pendant is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be found in the High Entia Tomb, at the northernmost dead end room on the first basement floor. When the area is approached three enemies appear. It is required for Dream of a Poet in Colony 6 and only appears once the quest is triggered.
Summon Copy (Japanese: , Samoningukopī) is one of Melia's summon arts in and . It summons a copy of the most recently summoned element, even if that element has already been discharged.
